searchText: <@360491619402776577> do you have a specific dos attack that motivated the no-nonce-gaps design in geth's blob pool? We also have that requirement but I cannot think of a dos vector that would exploit a pool without the requirement or I guess <@206016661470314496> is in here too Yep, I give you 10 nonce gapped transactions from every account The transactions will never be executable I churn them with 10 higher paying transactions from other accounts I see, isn't the same attack possible with e.g low fee blob txs? Yep, but they can become executable if the fees drop Also if you churn them with higher paying transactions, they will be executable at some point right, because of the bump req hmmmm, with 3074 you could also sweep accounts in the txpool with a single tx still not sure whether or not this would change anything in our pool impl Yes and thats something we've been discussing We have a test for it and it takes ~1 sec to reorg the txs out of our pool, but that is very dependent on our pool implementation (we don't delete transactions, we just tombstone them) oh interesting, could i have a link to the test? depends on how you revalidate the pool. unless you're doing something really fancy it's probably fine yeah I just checked, shouldn't require any changes, we discard based on balance changes already https://github.com/MariusVanDerWijden/go-ethereum/tree/blob-test

excerpts.author: rjected
excerpts.content: <@360491619402776577> do you have a specific dos attack that motivated the no-nonce-gaps design in geth's blob pool? We also have that requirement but I cannot think of a dos vector that would exploit a pool without the requirement

excerpts.author: rjected
excerpts.content: or I guess <@206016661470314496> is in here too

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Yep, I give you 10 nonce gapped transactions from every account

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: The transactions will never be executable

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: I churn them with 10 higher paying transactions from other accounts

excerpts.author: rjected
excerpts.content: I see, isn't the same attack possible with e.g low fee blob txs?

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Yep, but they can become executable if the fees drop

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Also if you churn them with higher paying transactions, they will be executable at some point

excerpts.author: rjected
excerpts.content: right, because of the bump req

excerpts.author: rjected
excerpts.content: hmmmm, with 3074 you could also sweep accounts in the txpool with a single tx

excerpts.author: rjected
excerpts.content: still not sure whether or not this would change anything in our pool impl

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Yes and thats something we've been discussing

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: We have a test for it and it takes ~1 sec to reorg the txs out of our pool, but that is very dependent on our pool implementation (we don't delete transactions, we just tombstone them)

excerpts.author: rjected
excerpts.content: oh interesting, could i have a link to the test?

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: depends on how you revalidate the pool. unless you're doing something really fancy it's probably fine

excerpts.author: rjected
excerpts.content: yeah I just checked, shouldn't require any changes, we discard based on balance changes already
